segments.note: Chartered 1852 as the independent Buffalo and Lockport Railroad, completed 1853 - the same year it became one of ten constituent railroads consolidated to form the original New York Central Railroad. Lockport, on the Erie Canal, had earlier been served by the separate (bankrupt) Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad (1834-38) and the Rochester, Lockport and Niagara Falls Railroad (opened 1852); this line gave it a direct rail connection to Buffalo instead. Passenger service wound down like the rest of the NYC system through the mid-20th century; Lockport was never part of the Amtrak network. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
